acquaint.clue: To introduce someone to a subject so they know it firsthand.
acquaint.explanation: This verb means giving someone their first direct knowledge of something. You might do it with a new city, a new job, or an unfamiliar set of rules.

activity.clue: The busy, energetic motion of a place that is far from still.
activity.explanation: In this sense the word means vigorous movement or bustle rather than one particular task. A crowded market at midday is full of it.

admonish.clue: To warn someone gently but seriously about a fault or oversight.
admonish.explanation: This is a mild but earnest correction, not an angry telling-off. A teacher might do this to a pupil who keeps forgetting homework.

adventure.clue: An exciting or remarkable experience, often involving travel and risk.
adventure.explanation: The word names an experience worth retelling because it was thrilling or unusual. It suggests something out of the ordinary rather than everyday routine.

ambitious.clue: Driven by a strong wish to succeed, gain power, or become famous.
ambitious.explanation: This describes a person shaped by a hunger for achievement. It can be admiring or slightly critical, depending on how far the hunger goes.

ambivalent.clue: Holding two opposite feelings about the same thing at once.
ambivalent.explanation: The word describes genuinely mixed feelings, not simple indifference. In the dictionary example it pairs with "conflicted" to describe how someone feels about their job.

architect.clue: The professional who plans a building and advises on its construction.
architect.explanation: This person designs structures and guides how they get built. The word is also used figuratively for whoever devised a plan or system.

atlantis.clue: A legendary island said to have vanished beneath the waves long ago.
atlantis.explanation: This is a fabled island from ancient legend, believed to have sunk into the ocean. It has become a byword for any lost civilisation.

available.clue: Ready to be had or used, because nothing is blocking access.
available.explanation: The word means something can be reached, obtained, or used right now. It applies equally to a free seat, a product in stock, or a person with spare time.

awkward.clue: Lacking grace or ease, the way a stumble looks when someone lands badly.
awkward.explanation: In this sense the word describes clumsy movement rather than social discomfort. The dictionary example uses it for a bad landing that nearly caused injury.

backstage.clue: Relating to the hidden area of a theatre where performers prepare.
backstage.explanation: As an adjective this describes the part of a theatre the audience never sees, including the dressing rooms. It is also used for anything happening out of public view.

bellwether.clue: Something watched closely because it signals which way a trend is heading.
bellwether.explanation: The word names an early indicator of change. Analysts often call one company or one district by this name when its results predict a wider pattern.

bituminous.clue: Describing a substance containing or soaked with natural pitch.
bituminous.explanation: This adjective describes material that contains a thick black petroleum residue. It is most often heard describing a soft, high-carbon type of coal.

bookshelf.clue: An open ledge in a room where volumes stand side by side.
bookshelf.explanation: This is a single open shelf made for holding reading material. Unlike a cupboard it has no doors, so everything on it stays visible.

caffeine.clue: The bitter compound in coffee and tea that keeps you awake.
caffeine.explanation: This is a naturally occurring bitter substance found in coffee, tea, cacao and kola nuts. It is used medically as a stimulant and a diuretic.

cardiovascular.clue: Relating to the heart together with the vessels that carry blood.
cardiovascular.explanation: The adjective covers the heart and the whole network of vessels serving it. You will meet it most often in medicine and in fitness training.

challenge.clue: A task hard enough to test whoever decides to take it on.
challenge.explanation: Used as a noun, the word names a difficult task or problem. In the dictionary example, finding a venue that met every requirement turned out to be one.

chancellor.clue: The chief minister leading the government in several European nations.
chancellor.explanation: In this sense the word names the highest minister of state in certain European countries. Germany and Austria both use the title for their head of government.

chemistry.clue: The science of what substances are made of and how they change.
chemistry.explanation: This field studies the composition and structure of substances, and the transformations they undergo. It sits between physics and biology in the sciences.

chimpanzee.clue: A clever African ape, smaller than a gorilla and more at home in trees.
chimpanzee.explanation: This is a great ape native to equatorial Africa. It is smaller than a gorilla and spends far more of its time up in the branches.

colloquy.clue: A formal conversation or exchange of views between people.
colloquy.explanation: The word means a talk or discussion, usually a fairly formal one. It is more literary than the everyday words for the same thing.

comfortable.clue: Feeling settled and secure, with nothing pressing to worry about.
comfortable.explanation: The word covers both giving and enjoying a sense of contentment and security. A chair can be described this way, and so can the person sitting in it.

commitment.clue: A promise given now to do something at a later time.
commitment.explanation: This sense of the word means an agreement or promise about future action. The dictionary example describes an athlete giving a spoken one to a team.

consistent.clue: Staying the same from one time to the next, without contradiction.
consistent.explanation: This describes something marked by regularity and free from variation. The dictionary example notes that many Americans once wrote their own names differently from one document to the next.

contest.clue: A struggle between rivals to see which one comes out on top.
contest.explanation: As a noun the word names a struggle for victory or superiority. Note that the verb form, meaning to dispute something, is a separate use.

conversation.clue: A spoken exchange in which people share ideas and opinions.
conversation.explanation: The word means talk in which observations and ideas actually pass between people. One dictionary example draws a sharp line between mere talk and this.

correspondence.clue: Communication carried on by written messages sent back and forth.
correspondence.explanation: In this sense the word means communication by letters or email. It can name the activity itself or the collected messages that resulted.

criticize.clue: To point out what is wrong with someone or something.
criticize.explanation: This verb means finding fault and saying so. It does not have to be unfair, though it usually carries a negative tone.

deception.clue: The act of making someone believe something that is not true.
deception.explanation: The word names the act of causing another person to accept something false as though it were true. It implies intent rather than honest error.

definitely.clue: In a way that leaves no room for doubt or ambiguity.
definitely.explanation: This adverb signals certainty and the absence of any vagueness. In the dictionary example it emphasises how firmly the speaker holds their view of an actor.

dictionary.clue: A reference source listing words with meanings and pronunciations.
dictionary.explanation: This is a reference work, printed or electronic, that lists words alphabetically. Each entry adds information such as pronunciation, origin and meaning.

disparage.clue: To speak of someone or something as if it had little worth.
disparage.explanation: The verb means talking about something slightingly, lowering its apparent value. The dictionary example shows novels being dismissed with a contemptuous label.

divulge.clue: To make known a secret you were expected to keep.
divulge.explanation: This verb means revealing information that was private or confidential. It carries a sense that the information was not yours to share.

effervescent.clue: Lively and sparkling in personality, like a drink full of bubbles.
effervescent.explanation: Beyond fizzing liquids, the word describes an appealingly lively manner. The dictionary example applies it to someone who handled the press with fresh, direct energy.

encyclopedia.clue: A large reference set with articles on every branch of learning.
encyclopedia.explanation: This is a work covering all branches of knowledge, or treating one branch thoroughly. Articles are usually arranged alphabetically by subject.

epistemology.clue: The branch of philosophy asking how we know what we claim to know.
epistemology.explanation: This field studies the nature and grounds of knowledge, especially its limits and how far it can be trusted. It is one of the central areas of philosophy.

eschatology.clue: The branch of theology dealing with the end of the world.
eschatology.explanation: This part of theology concerns final events in the history of the world or of humankind. Different faiths give it very different content.

ethereal.clue: Delicate and light in a way that seems to come from another world.
ethereal.explanation: The word suggests something too fine or unearthly to belong here. The dictionary example uses it for the glow a rising full moon casts on a wild shore.

euphoria.clue: An intense feeling of happiness and well-being that lifts you up.
euphoria.explanation: This names a strong sense of well-being or joy. Its opposite, a state of unease and dissatisfaction, has its own separate name.

existentialism.clue: A philosophy centred on individual freedom and responsibility in an uncertain universe.
existentialism.explanation: This mainly twentieth-century movement gathers several different doctrines. What they share is a focus on the individual who must take responsibility for free choices without certain moral knowledge.

expertise.clue: The deep skill someone has after long practice in one field.
expertise.explanation: The word names the specialised skill of someone highly trained in a subject. It refers to the ability itself, not the person who holds it.

exquisite.clue: So finely made or beautiful that it seems close to perfect.
exquisite.explanation: This describes something that pleases through its beauty or its perfect fitness for purpose. It suggests fine detail rather than sheer scale.

fallacy.clue: A mistaken belief, especially one built on faulty reasoning.
fallacy.explanation: The word names a false or mistaken idea. The dictionary example points to the error of treating a threat and a capability as the same thing.

fluorescent.clue: Giving off a bright glow when light strikes it.
fluorescent.explanation: This adjective describes something bright and glowing because it re-emits the light it absorbs. Safety vests and tube lighting are everyday examples.

gemstone.clue: A mineral cut and polished so it can be set into jewellery.
gemstone.explanation: This is a mineral or petrified material valuable enough to cut and polish for ornament. Cutting is what turns the raw material into one.

gnarled.clue: Twisted and full of knots, the way an ancient tree trunk looks.
gnarled.explanation: The word describes a rough, twisted surface covered in hard lumps. It suits old trees and weathered hands equally well.

hermeneutics.clue: The study of how texts, especially scripture, should be interpreted.
hermeneutics.explanation: This field examines the principles behind interpretation itself. It began with biblical study and now reaches into law, literature and philosophy.

homesick.clue: Sad and longing for your own house and family while far away.
homesick.explanation: The word describes the ache of missing your familiar surroundings during an absence. Students and travellers meet it often in their first weeks away.

illuminate.clue: To fill a dark place with light so things become visible.
illuminate.explanation: In this sense the verb means supplying or brightening something with light. A related figurative use means making an idea clearer.

insistent.clue: Repeating a demand firmly and refusing to be brushed aside.
insistent.explanation: This describes someone or something that keeps pressing a point. It can apply to a person, a knock at the door, or a repeating musical phrase.

instagram.clue: To share a photograph on a well-known picture-based social network.
instagram.explanation: Used as a verb, this means posting a picture to a particular photo-sharing service. The dictionary example describes people doing it with cherry blossoms in spring.

instruction.clue: A written outline telling you the steps for doing something.
instruction.explanation: In this sense the word names an outline or manual of technical procedure. It usually appears in the plural on the leaflet inside a box.

irrevocable.clue: Impossible to undo or take back once it has been done.
irrevocable.explanation: This describes a decision or action that cannot be reversed. Legal documents use it to make clear that no one may change their mind later.

jacuzzi.clue: A heated tub with jets of swirling water for relaxing in.
jacuzzi.explanation: This is a trademark used for a bath or small pool with powerful water jets. Like several brand names, it is often used loosely for any similar tub.

jerusalem.clue: An ancient Middle Eastern city sacred to three major religions.
jerusalem.explanation: This city in south-western Asia lies north-west of the Dead Sea. It has been a capital since ancient times and is holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims.

jocund.clue: Cheerful and full of light-hearted high spirits.
jocund.explanation: The word suggests brightness of mood and lively good humour. It is old-fashioned now and turns up mostly in poetry.

knowledge.clue: What you have gained through learning and experience over time.
knowledge.explanation: The word covers information, understanding and skill, however they were acquired. Both schooling and lived experience produce it.

laminate.clue: To join thin sheets together into one stronger material.
laminate.explanation: As a verb this means uniting layers with adhesive or another method. Plywood and identity cards are both made this way.

language.clue: The system of words a community uses to speak and write.
language.explanation: The word covers words, how they sound, how they are written and how they combine. What makes it work is that a whole community shares the system.

lavender.clue: A fragrant purple-flowered plant grown for its scent and oil.
lavender.explanation: This Mediterranean plant of the mint family has narrow leaves and lilac-purple spikes. It is dried for sachets and pressed for oil used in perfume.

legend.clue: A story handed down from long ago, perhaps true, perhaps not.
legend.explanation: The word names a story that has come down from the past. Whether the events really happened is usually beyond proving.

library.clue: A place holding volumes and recordings for borrowing rather than buying.
library.explanation: This is a place keeping written, musical and reference material for people to use. The key point is that the material is lent out, not sold.

literature.clue: Writing in prose or verse, valued as an art form.
literature.explanation: The word covers writing in either prose or verse. In a narrower use it means only the writing considered to have lasting artistic worth.

locomotion.clue: The power or act of moving from one place to another.
locomotion.explanation: The word names both the ability to move about and the act itself. Biologists use it for how animals travel, whether by walking, swimming or flight.

loquacious.clue: Fond of talking at great length, often more than needed.
loquacious.explanation: This describes someone given to fluent or excessive talk. The dictionary example uses it, with understatement, of a man who says little to reporters.

manipulate.clue: To control someone by unfair or sneaky means for your own gain.
manipulate.explanation: In this sense the verb means controlling a person through artful or underhand methods. The dictionary example describes someone used this way by those around him.

melancholy.clue: A settled, thoughtful sadness that hangs over someone's mood.
melancholy.explanation: As a noun this names a state of low spirits and sadness. The dictionary example describes a singer turning that feeling into tender art.

misanthrope.clue: Someone with a deep distrust and dislike of people in general.
misanthrope.explanation: This names a person who hates or mistrusts humankind as a whole. The dislike is general rather than aimed at any particular individual.

mountain.clue: A great mass of rock rising far above the land around it.
mountain.explanation: This is a landmass standing conspicuously above its surroundings and taller than a hill. Where exactly the line falls between the two varies by country.

myopia.clue: The eye condition that makes distant objects look blurred.
myopia.explanation: In this condition images focus in front of the retina rather than on it, so far-off things look unclear. The word is also used for short-term thinking.

mystery.clue: Something that stays unexplained no matter how hard you think.
mystery.explanation: The word names something not understood, or perhaps beyond understanding altogether. It can describe a puzzle awaiting a solution or one that admits none.

nefarious.clue: Openly wicked, in the way a storybook schemer plots harm.
nefarious.explanation: The word means flagrantly evil or corrupt, with no attempt at concealment. The dictionary example applies it to the worst supervillains, who hide in plain sight.

novelist.clue: A writer whose work takes the form of long invented stories.
novelist.explanation: This names someone who writes book-length works of fiction. A writer of short stories or poetry is described by a different word.

onomatopoeia.clue: The way certain words copy the very sound they describe.
onomatopoeia.explanation: This is the naming of a thing or action by imitating the sound it makes. Buzz and hiss are standard examples.

ornithology.clue: The scientific study of birds and their behaviour.
ornithology.explanation: This is the branch of zoology devoted to birds. It covers their classification, habits, migration and song.

oxygen.clue: The gas making up a fifth of the air, which keeps us alive.
oxygen.explanation: This chemical element has atomic number eight and forms twenty-one percent of the atmosphere. Almost every known organism depends on it, and it drives combustion.

oxymoron.clue: A phrase that pairs two words which contradict each other.
oxymoron.explanation: This is a combination of incongruous words, such as cruel kindness. The dictionary example notes that the point is the contradictory feeling behind it, not just the wordplay.

panoply.clue: A full and impressive display of everything on show at once.
panoply.explanation: The word names a magnificent or striking array. The dictionary example uses it for woods showing their whole spread of autumn foliage.

parenthesis.clue: One of the pair of curved marks that enclose an aside.
parenthesis.explanation: This names one or both of the curved marks used to enclose an inserted remark. Mathematics uses the same marks to group symbols together.

patricide.clue: The killing of one's own father.
patricide.explanation: The word names the murder of a father by his own child. Related words describe the killing of a mother or a brother.

peacock.clue: A bird famous for spreading a shimmering fan of tail feathers.
peacock.explanation: This is the male of a bird known for its crest and its long, loosely webbed tail coverts. The fan is spread mainly to attract a mate.

pickle.clue: A cucumber kept in brine or vinegar so it lasts.
pickle.explanation: In this sense the word names a preserved cucumber. The same word can describe the preserving liquid, and informally a difficult situation.

pineapple.clue: A spiky tropical fruit with sweet yellow flesh inside.
pineapple.explanation: This is the large edible fruit of a tropical plant, formed from many flowers fused together. That fusion is why the skin looks so distinctly patterned.

playful.clue: Light-hearted and full of fun rather than serious.
playful.explanation: The word describes a humorous, teasing manner. It suits a joke made in good spirit or a kitten batting at a piece of string.

poltergeist.clue: A ghost blamed for banging sounds and objects that move themselves.
poltergeist.explanation: This names a mischievous spirit said to cause unexplained noises such as rapping. The name comes from German words for a knocking ghost.

possessed.clue: Completely controlled by a spirit, a passion, or a fixed idea.
possessed.explanation: The adjective describes someone overwhelmingly ruled by an outside force. That force might be supernatural, but it can equally be an obsession.

prestigious.clue: Highly respected and carrying great standing in its field.
prestigious.explanation: This describes something honoured and widely admired. Universities, awards and journals are often described this way.

probably.clue: In all likelihood, though without complete certainty.
probably.explanation: This adverb marks something as reasonably expected to be true, but not guaranteed. It leaves a little room for being wrong.

punishment.clue: Suffering or loss imposed on someone as payment for wrongdoing.
punishment.explanation: The word names suffering, pain or loss that serves as retribution. The idea of deserved payment is what separates it from mere misfortune.

puzzle.clue: A game or problem made deliberately hard to work out.
puzzle.explanation: This names something designed to be challenging to answer or solve. Crosswords and jigsaws are familiar kinds.

quintessential.clue: Being the purest and most typical example of its kind.
quintessential.explanation: The word describes something perfectly representative of a type. The dictionary example applies it to a streetwise New Yorker.

regenerate.clue: Formed once more, as though made new a second time.
regenerate.explanation: Used as an adjective, this describes something formed or created again. Note that the verb, meaning to grow back, is a separate use.

rhythmic.clue: Moving with a strong, regular beat you can feel.
rhythmic.explanation: The adjective describes something marked by a pronounced repeating pattern in time. Drums, waves and breathing can all be described this way.

scared.clue: Filled with fear, the way a sudden noise leaves you.
scared.explanation: The word describes being thrown into a state of fear or panic. It covers everything from mild alarm to genuine terror.

schadenfreude.clue: The guilty pleasure of enjoying someone else's misfortune.
schadenfreude.explanation: Borrowed from German, this names the enjoyment taken in hearing about others' troubles. The dictionary example describes it spreading unpleasantly across social media.

solitude.clue: The state of being entirely alone, away from other people.
solitude.explanation: The word names being alone or remote from society. Unlike loneliness it need not be unhappy, and is often chosen deliberately.

student.clue: Someone who attends a school in order to learn.
student.explanation: This names a person enrolled at a school. In wider use it can mean anyone making a careful study of a subject.

supersede.clue: To take over the place of something older and set it aside.
supersede.explanation: The verb means taking the position of something that came before. A new edition does this to the one it follows.

variant.clue: A form that differs a little from the standard type.
variant.explanation: As a noun this names something showing variation from a norm. The dictionary example refers to a differing form of a particular gene.

victorious.clue: Having come out the winner in a contest or battle.
victorious.explanation: The adjective describes whoever has won. It applies to teams, armies and arguments alike.

vocabulary.clue: The whole store of words a person or language uses.
vocabulary.explanation: The word names the sum of words used by a language, a group, an individual or a field. Yours grows every time you learn a new one.

wondrous.clue: So extraordinary that it fills you with amazement.
wondrous.explanation: This describes something to be marvelled at. It is a slightly poetic word, more at home in stories than in conversation.

xenophobia.clue: A deep fear and hatred of people from other countries.
xenophobia.explanation: The word names fear and hatred of strangers or foreigners, or of anything foreign. It comes from Greek roots meaning stranger and fear.

zeitgeist.clue: The mood and outlook that defines a particular period in history.
zeitgeist.explanation: Borrowed from German, this names the general intellectual, moral and cultural climate of an era. Each decade is often said to have its own.

zygote.clue: The single cell formed when two reproductive cells join.
zygote.explanation: This is the cell produced by the union of two gametes. Every animal that reproduces sexually begins as one.
